title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The surrounding pages build a group, written G_{0,3}, as an extension of the free group Pi_{0,3} = pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}). Pi_{0,3} is extended by the S_3 symmetries of {0,1,inf} and by complex conjugation tau. The previous page identifies G_{0,3} as the Coxeter group generated by three 'fundamental reflections' r_0 = tau'_inf, r_1 = tau'_0, r_inf = tau_inf. Its relations are r_i^2 = (r_0 r_inf)^2 = (r_1 r_0)^3 = 1. The orientation-preserving subgroup G^+_{0,3} has presentation sigma_inf^2 = rho^3 = 1, i.e. Z/2 * Z/3.

This page does three things.

(34) It writes the remarkable elements of G^+ in terms of sigma_inf and rho:
- epsilon_0 = sigma_inf rho, epsilon_1 = rho sigma_inf, epsilon_inf = rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho^{-1}. These are the parabolic 'half-loops' around 0, 1, inf.
- lambda_i = epsilon_i^2 are the loops themselves, i.e. generators of Pi_{0,3}.

(35) It writes the conjugate involutions sigma_0 = rho sigma_inf rho^{-1} and sigma_1 = rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho, and re-expresses them through the epsilons.

(36) It writes the other reflections as words in r_0, r_1, r_inf, using rho = r_0 r_1:
- tau_0 = rho tau_inf rho^{-1} = r_0 r_1 r_inf r_1 r_0;
- tau_1 = rho^{-1} tau_inf rho = r_1 r_0 r_inf r_0 r_1;
- tau'_1 = rho tau'_0 rho^{-1} = r_0 r_1 r_0.

Section IV begins the identification with PGL(2,Z) = GL(2,Z)/±1. Formula (37) gives the action on the upper half-plane: Möbius for det +1, anti-Möbius (via z-bar) for det -1.
- The fundamental domain is the hyperbolic triangle with vertices i, e^{i pi/3} = -j-bar and inf, i.e. 0 <= Re z <= 1/2, |z| >= 1.
- This hyperbolic triangle corresponds, under the modular lambda-function D -> P^1 - {0,1,inf} (quotient by Gamma(2)), to the triangle on the Riemann sphere with vertices 1/2, -j-bar and 0. Under this correspondence i -> 1/2, -j-bar -> -j-bar, inf -> 0.
- Formula (38) gives the reflections in its sides: r_0(z) = 1/z-bar (unit circle), r_1(z) = 1 - z-bar (Re z = 1/2), r_inf(z) = -z-bar (Re z = 0).

The next page completes the isomorphism G_{0,3} ≅ PGL(2,Z), the (2,3,inf) extended triangle group, and G^+_{0,3} ≅ PSL(2,Z). The purpose is to fix explicit, sign-careful formulas ('formulaire') for the lowest level (0,3) of the Teichmüller tower, as a base for the later study of the 'équation des lacets' (the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations).
errors: In (34) the expansion of lambda_inf appears as rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho^{-1}. But (rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho^{-1})^2 = rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho^{-2} sigma_inf rho^{-1} = rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho sigma_inf rho^{-1}, since rho^3 = 1. In Z/2*Z/3 these differ, so the middle exponent is a slip, unless the manuscript actually has rho there (hard to read).

Minor point: the hatched domain is a hyperbolic triangle. 'Triangle sphérique' refers to its image on the Riemann sphere under the lambda-function, which is consistent; the identification map is only named loosely ('homomorphisme de variété').

ideas.what: Extended modular group PGL(2,Z) as the reflection group of the (2,3,inf) hyperbolic triangle, with explicit reflections 1/z-bar, 1 - z-bar, -z-bar and Coxeter presentation
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group as (2,3,inf) Coxeter/triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein, Fricke, Poincaré (19th century); standard textbook material
ideas.where_published: PSL(2,Z) and the lowest levels of the Teichmüller tower appear in Esquisse d'un programme; this explicit reflection presentation is unsure

ideas.what: Identification of the extension of pi_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}) by S_3 (and complex conjugation) with PSL(2,Z) (resp. PGL(2,Z)), via the lambda-function D -> M_{0,4} = H/Gamma(2)
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of M_{0,4}/S_3, i.e. Gamma(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL(2,Z) with quotient S_3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Jacobi/Klein lambda function); in the GT context Drinfeld and Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and the modular group informally

ideas.what: Explicit dictionary of 'half-loops' epsilon_i, loops lambda_i = epsilon_i^2, involutions sigma_i and reflections tau_i, tau'_i as words in sigma_inf, rho or in r_0, r_1, r_inf
ideas.modern_name: Explicit generators of PSL(2,Z) and PGL(2,Z) adapted to the three cusps (bookkeeping for GT relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; similar bookkeeping in Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely classical bookkeeping: the Coxeter presentation of PGL(2,Z) as the (2,3,inf) reflection group and its link to P^1 minus 3 points with S_3 symmetry. It is useful context for the 'équation des lacets' but contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Triangle vertices: likely '(-j-bar, i, inf)' in D corresponding to '(-j-bar, 1/2, 0)' on the sphere, not '(-j, i, inf^{1/2})'. Here -j-bar = e^{i pi/3}.
The group in the line before (36) appears as G^-_{0,3} (with a superscript) in the image, i.e. the full group including orientation-reversing elements.
In (36) the third line reads tau'_1 = rho tau'_0 rho^{-1} = tau'_inf tau'_0 tau'_inf (= r_0 r_1 r_0).
In (35) the crossed-out exponents on rho (rho^4, rho^{4-1}) are struck through; the intended formulas are sigma_0 = rho sigma_inf rho^{-1} and sigma_1 = rho^{-1} sigma_inf rho.
'homomorphisme de variété' may be 'homéomorphisme'; the intended map is the lambda-function / Gamma(2)-quotient D -> P^1 - {0,1,inf}.
